title: Count the ways to climb n steps
summary: Count the different ways to climb a staircase taking one or two steps at a time, by writing an answer on every step.
goal: Count the different ways to reach the top step

mapping.formal: Last move from step i − 1 or i − 2

examples.label: Five steps
examples.explanation: 8 different sequences of 1s and 2s add up to 5.

ladder.name: Try every path
ladder.idea: Recursively try a 1-step and a 2-step move from each step and count the paths that land exactly on the top.

ladder.name: A note on every step
ladder.idea: Write on each step how many ways reach it: the ways to reach the step below plus the ways to reach the step two below.
ladder.insight: The brute force asks "how many ways reach step 3?" again and again. Writing each answer down once means every step is worked out exactly once.

ladder.name: Keep only the last two notes
ladder.idea: Each note only uses the two notes before it, so keep just those two numbers and roll them forward.
ladder.insight: Once step i is written, notes below i − 1 are never read again. Two variables are enough.

approaches.name: A note on every step
approaches.summary: Fill ways[i] = ways[i − 1] + ways[i − 2] from the bottom up.

transfer.problem: Tiling a 2 × n path with 1 × 2 paving slabs, laid either across or as a pair along: how many layouts are there?
transfer.explanation: The last slab either covers one column (across) or two columns (a pair), so layouts(n) = layouts(n − 1) + layouts(n − 2): the same recurrence.

selfCheck: Sets both base cases: one way to stand on step 0 and one way to reach step 1.
Adds the two previous answers for each step.
Does not recompute the same step twice.
